root_cause: The bounded full-site visibility fix replaced sequential route iteration with worker-based route concurrency, but an older website release-risk regression still required the removed sequential loop shape.
The implementation regression and the older release-risk oracle were not cochanged, so unrelated website PRs inherited a deterministic baseline failure after the concurrency fix reached main.

The GitHub website browser lane invoked standalone-visibility-check.mjs without an OS-level process timeout, so a Playwright/browser protocol wedge could outlive the script's internal route budget and retain a runner.
prevention: Any implementation-shape change in the visibility verifier must cochange every regression that asserts that shape.
The canonical brain boundedness regression now verifies the runtime concurrency contract and the website release-risk oracle together.
Do not rerun or rebuild multiple affected PRs until the shared main regression is fixed once.
Learning canonicalization accepts only classified tests/brain-*.test.mjs evaluation paths; non-Brain implementation tests remain supporting evidence, never canonical evaluation references.
Every full-site browser verifier must have both an internal semantic time budget and an outer OS-level hard timeout materially below the enclosing job timeout.
